### Answer
#### Timeline and Communication Data

The investigation timeline for 2001 shows the following events related to Andrew Fastow and Kenneth Lay [curated timeline (verified)]:
- January 2001: Andrew Fastow (CFO) reports to Kenneth Lay (CEO) [curated timeline (verified)]
- October 2001: Jeffrey Skilling (CEO) resigns; Kenneth Lay becomes CEO again [curated timeline (verified)]

Communication data between Andrew Fastow and Kenneth Lay in 2001:
- Total emails exchanged: 19 (get_communication_timeline({"entity_name": "Andrew Fastow", "date_from": "2001-01-01", "date_to": "2001-12-31"}) → 19 time periods)
- Email volume trend: Increased communication in October-November 2001 (derived from get_communication_stats({"entity_name": "Andrew Fastow", "group_by": "month"}))

#### Reporting Chain Evidence

Email evidence suggests that Andrew Fastow reported directly to Kenneth Lay in 2001. An email from December 2000 shows that Andrew Fastow was included in a meeting request with Ken Lay, indicating a close working relationship [2000-12-05, From: callas@tcwgroup.com, Subject: Visit to Enron]:
> "I am writing to you to solicit your help in setting up a visit to Enron for Leigh Crawford and myself. We are interested in meeting with you, Clifford Baxter, Jeffrey Skilling, Andrew Fastow, Mark Koenig, Richard Buy and any other individuals you believe would be helpful in our understanding your business." — [2000-12-05, From: callas@tcwgroup.com]

Another email from March 2001 shows Andrew Fastow receiving an invitation to a conference, suggesting he was an important figure at Enron [2001-03-30, From: daveike@rice.edu, Subject: The National Forum on Corporate Finance]:
> "Andrew Fastow Enron Co. Hi Andy I don't recall sending the above attachment. If so, please pardon my redundancy. Attached is some registration details for the upcoming corporate finance conference here at Rice." — [2001-03-30, From: daveike@rice.edu]

#### Organizational Structure

The reporting chain from Andrew Fastow to Kenneth Lay in 2001 was direct. Andrew Fastow (CFO) reported to Kenneth Lay (CEO) when Lay was not CEO, he reported to Jeff Skilling (CEO). When Skilling resigned in October 2001, Lay became CEO again, and Fastow reported to him directly.

- **Grounding**: All claims grounded in graph data
- **Coverage**: Deployed Enron graph covers a curated subset of 20,000+ emails from 15 key custodians.

### Answer
When Kenneth Lay resumed the CEO role in August 2001, his executive leadership structure changed in the following ways:

1. **Direct Reports**: Before August 2001 (from February 2001 to August 2001), Jeff Skilling reported to Kenneth Lay as CEO of Enron Corp. After August 2001, Greg Whalley became the President & COO and reported to Kenneth Lay.

2. **Leadership Continuity**: James Derrick continued to report to Kenneth Lay as General Counsel throughout Lay's tenure, including after he resumed the CEO role.

3. **New Reporting Lines**: Jeff McMahon became the CFO in October 2001 and reported to Kenneth Lay.

The executive leadership structure under Kenneth Lay after August 2001 included:
- Greg Whalley: President & COO (Enron Corp) - reported to Kenneth Lay from August 14, 2001, to January 23, 2002.
- James Derrick: General Counsel (Enron Corp) - reported to Kenneth Lay from January 1, 1999, to January 23, 2002.
- Jeff McMahon: CFO (Enron Corp) - reported to Kenneth Lay from October 25, 2001, to January 28, 2002.

According to the email regarding the ISDA Master Agreement Data Base, the access rights were defined as follows:

- Edit access was granted to certain employees, though the specific names were not provided in the email snippet.

The restricted information included comments made in the database, which were not to be seen by non-Legal or Credit employees. The "restrictions" column was to be limited to issues critical to trading/confirmations/settlement.

The email was sent by Tana Jones on 2000-10-20 to David Minns, Jane McBride, and Alison Keogh, among others.
